Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold, as this may cause feedback into the conference. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Strategy Officer; and Robert Kim, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, operating margin by segment, supply costs and other operating expenses, initiatives to improve operating margin, operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, and capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter and full year.

On net patient revenue, we saw strong growth reflecting volume recovery and payer mix improvements. Inpatient volumes stabilized while outpatient surged, highlighting our shift to higher-margin ambulatory care. Margins varied by segment, with ambulatory and behavioral health leading. Supply costs moderated through optimization efforts, and our margin improvement programs delivered meaningful savings. We're guiding margins higher ahead and investing capex prudently for growth.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $4.28 billion, an increase of 7.8% compared to the same period last year and 2.9% quarter-over-quarter. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Let me start by diving deeper into our net patient revenue performance, which underscores the strength across our 52-hospital footprint spanning 12 states. Quarter-over-quarter, we grew $121 million from Q2's $4.16 billion, fueled by a 1.8% uptick in total admissions to 142,500—our strongest print since early 2022—along with a 2.1% rise in inpatient equivalent days and a case mix index improvement to 1.87 from 1.84, reflecting more complex cardiac and neuro cases. Outpatient revenue, now 58% of the total, jumped 4.2% to $2.48 billion on 6.1% higher observation and outpatient visits to 1.12 million, boosted by three new ASCs in Texas and Florida capturing Medicare Advantage volume.

Year-over-year, the 7.8% growth outpaced peers, with admissions up 3.2%, ED visits climbing 4.7% to 2.45 million thanks to AI triage reducing door-to-doc times by 18%, and outpatient volumes exploding 8.4%, or 11.2% in our HOPDs and freestanding ERs. CMI expanded 2.6% on 5.1% surgical growth in high-value MS-DRGs like major joints, revenue per admission rose 4.4% to $22,450 despite flat Medicare rates from IPPS adjustments, offset by 5.8% commercial pricing gains. Regionally, Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida drove 9.2% growth on population influx and Medicaid shifts, while Midwest was more modest at 4.1%.

Our payer mix remained steady at 42% commercial, 28% Medicare, 18% Medicaid, and 12% managed care/MA, with net revenue per admission up 1.1% QoQ from Epic RCM rollout cutting days in A/R to 45.3 and clean claims to 97.1%. This affirms our high-acuity strategy, with $250 million capex fueling OR expansions and robotics for CMI lift, plus $85 million clawed back via audits. We see 5-7% Q4 growth from seasonal volumes and MA improvements.

Transitioning to trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, this dynamic is central to our performance across our 42 acute care hospitals and 120+ outpatient sites, especially in Sunbelt and Midwest markets. Total volumes grew 8.2% YoY, but outpatients dominated: inpatient adjusted admissions at 142,000 were flat QoQ and down 1.4% YoY as elective rebound stabilized, with CMI steady at 1.85 on cardiology and oncology acuity, and ALOS down to 4.7 days. Outpatient encounters surged 14.7% YoY to 2.8 million, OPCs up 16.2% on 22% musculoskeletal growth shifted to 65 ASCs.

By service line, ortho volumes rose 19% with 65% in ASCs using Stryker Mako for same-day discharges, cardio outpatients up 12% via Medtronic TAVR, oncology infusions 11% on biosimilars. Sunbelt outpatient growth hit 18%, Texas at 24% on reimbursement parity, Florida stable via Optum bundles; Midwest at 11% with inpatient down 3.2%. Drivers include normalized electives, 9% revenue per case uplift to $1,450, 42% MA mix, Epic MyChart boosting utilization to 88%, telehealth at 15% of consults. Outpatients now 62% of volumes at 32% EBITDA margins versus inpatient 18%, targeting 70/30 by 2026 via ASC JVs, with Q4 outpatient 13-15% and inpatient flat to +1%.

Next, operating margins by segment reflect our diversified resilience amid labor and reimbursement pressures. Consolidated adjusted operating margin hit 8.2%, up 110 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ. Acute care hospitals, 62% of revenues at $2.1 billion, expanded to 6.8% or 150 bps better, CMI to 1.92 on 12% elective ortho/cardio surge to 105% pre-pandemic, Sunbelt at 9.2%, Northeast 4.5%; robotics in 80% ORs and Epic CDI cut denials 15%.

ASCs, post-Horizon acquisition to 120 centers, $450 million up 28%, margins 24.5% expanded 220 bps on 18% musculoskeletal growth, Texas/California at 27%; athenahealth RCM down A/R to 35 days. Behavioral health $320 million up 15%, 14.2% steady on 22% adolescent admissions, Southeast 16.5%, telehealth up 35%. Post-acute $280 million up 20%, 12.1% with 88% SNF occupancy, AI staffing down agency 18%. Outpatient/post-acute now 45% mix, guiding acute 7.0-7.5%, ASCs 24-25%, behavioral 14-15%, post-acute 11.5-12.5% for FY.

On supply costs and other operating expenses, consolidated supplies were $478 million or 17.8% of net patient revenues, up 140 bps YoY but down from Q2's 18.2%, with YoY $36 million rise from pharma inflation like 22% GLP-1 surge mitigated to 12% via Vizient and 340B ($45 million annualized), surgical implants up 11% to $162 million on 15% ortho/cardio volumes but 18% variance cut via standardization ($8 million saved), non-pharma steady at 3.7%. Northeast at 19.5%, Sunbelt 16.2% via HealthTrust rebates. Other op-ex $312 million or 11.6%, up 4.1% excluding recoveries, professional services $112 million up 7% on coding/prior auth, facilities $89 million up 5% on HVAC/energy.

Initiatives include Oracle Health AI inventory reducing stockouts 35%/waste 28% ($25 million FY save), UiPath RPA for AP, GPO renewals, captive pharmacy for 25% IVs, Intuitive co-dev for 8% savings. Q4 supplies 17.4-17.6%, op-ex 11.5%, with 210 bps leverage for 50-75 bps EBITDA expansion.

Our initiatives to improve operating margin drove 210 bps expansion to 12.8% consolidated, trailing 12-month 11.9% toward 12-13% FY and 15%+ long-term. From Margin Resilience Program ($450 million run-rate): labor (45% costs) agency down 61% to 7% via ShiftMed/Epic AI (96% fill, 25% OT cut, 1,200 RNs, 92% retention), labor % down 180 bps to 41.2% ($120 million save); supplies (22%) Vizient 6-8% concessions, Omnicell RFID cut stockouts 40% ($15 million YTD, 110 bps to 20.1%, $85 million); RCM Waystar denials to 6.8%, AR to 42, commercial to 48% ($65 million cash); clinical da Vinci 90% facilities, OR time down 18%, telehealth 25%, turnover 4.6/day (admissions +5.1%, ASC 28%).

Sunbelt 16% target, Northeast 10-11%; $200 million 2025 pipeline de-risks vs. 340B/Medicaid changes via home/behavioral tuck-ins.

Our operating margin in Q3 was 13.2%, up 110 bps YoY ahead of 12-13% range, on 4.2% acuity-adjusted admissions, 6% commercial growth, $45 million acquisition synergies. Q4 guide 14.0-15.0% (80-180 bps sequential), same-facility revenue 5.5-6.5% (inpatient 3-4%, observation 5%, outpatient 7-8% via five ASCs, CMI 1.85), Medicare 2.9%, commercial 180-190% Medicare, value-based 25% revenue ($120 million savings). Expenses 85.5-86.0%: labor 3.5-4.0% via Horizon Flex/AI (OT -12%, 1,200 clinicians), supplies/drugs +5% locked Vizient 6% save, robotic throughput +15%; RCM Waystar denials to 4.2% ($30 million cash). Sunbelt 16-17%, Midwest 13-14%, Northeast/West 11-12%. FY2025 14.5-15.5% (EBITDA 22-23%), $300 million MarginMax (supply digitization, telehealth 40%, ACO REACH 15%), two $400 million bolt-ons, risks labor/payer shifts.

Operating expenses were $3.65 billion, representing 85.3% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in revenue cycle and supply chain.

Net income for the quarter was $425 million, or $1.72 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

For capex, FY2024 was $825 million or 8.2% TTM revenue/115% depreciation. FY2025 guide $920-975 million (11-18% growth, 9-9.5% of $10.4-10.7 billion revenue), Q1 $225-245 million. Buckets: facilities 40-45% ($390-435 million) three micro-hospitals ($150 million Texas/Florida), four ASCs ($100 million); equipment 30-35% ($290-340 million) 25 MRIs/Varian, 15 da Vinci Xi; IT 15-20% ($145-190 million) Epic Phase 2/DAX (notes -40%), telehealth/Cerner; maintenance 10%. $1.40-1.50 EBITDA/$ spent, <3 year payback 70%, 85% ops funded. Sunbelt 70% facilities.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Heart Care Excellence Program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs, which now handle 25% of outpatient visits and have reduced length of stay in targeted procedures.

Following that, David Patel will provide an update on operational efficiency.

David Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including lean management processes and centralized supply chain protocols, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow, with bed turnover up to 4.6 per day and OR utilization at 68%.

Next, Jennifer Lee will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, David. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets like Dallas-Fort Worth and enhance our service offerings through joint ventures with physician groups and value-based care alliances like ACO REACH.

After that, Robert Kim will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Robert Kim:
Thank you, Jennifer. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including Phase 2 Epic rollout with AI documentation and predictive analytics to cut clinician burden and bolster interoperability under the 21st Century Cures Act.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

Robert Kim:
Good morning, Emily. Recent cybersecurity threats have been a top priority, but our proactive measures have had minimal operational impact. We've enhanced our posture with advanced threat detection, regular penetration testing, and segmented networks, ensuring no patient data breaches. Our $90 million IT investment this year, including Nuance DAX and Cerner analytics, has fortified defenses while maintaining 99.9% system uptime. We're compliant ahead of HHS curves and continue partnering with firms like CrowdStrike for real-time monitoring.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Liu with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Liu:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thanks, David. We're aggressively scaling telehealth to 40% of visits by 2025, integrating Zoom with Epic for seamless virtual care in primary, behavioral, and post-acute settings. RPM programs, using wearables and AI alerts, have reduced readmissions 20% in pilots and will expand to 50 facilities, targeting Medicare Advantage bundles. This lowers costs per encounter by 8% and boosts access in rural Sunbelt sites, aligning with value-based shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Jennifer Lee:
Absolutely, Rachel. Our partnerships, like JVs with USPI for ASCs and Optum for bundles, are pivotal. The five new ASCs added this year drive 7-8% outpatient growth, while ACO REACH with CMS targets 15% risk revenue, delivering $120 million shared savings YTD. Two pending $400 million bolt-ons in Texas/Florida will add high-margin capacity, funded internally, with ROIC over 12% and 200 bps margin uplift expected.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Gonzalez:
Sarah, could you elaborate on the supply cost initiatives and how they factor into your margin guidance?

Sarah Jenkins:
Sure, Mark. Our supply optimization—Vizient GPO, RFID inventory, captive pharmacy, and robotic consumables—saved $25 million YTD, bending costs to 17% of revenue. This, plus labor productivity, supports Q4 14-15% margins and FY2025 14.5-15.5%, with $300 million MarginMax delivering 100 bps expansion despite headwinds.

Michael Thompson:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
